content:
The last **total solar eclipse** before the year **2000** occurred on **February 26, 1998**.

### Key Details:
- **Date:** February 26, 1998
- **Type:** Total Solar Eclipse
- **Path of Totality:** Visible in parts of the **Caribbean, northern South America, and the Atlantic Ocean**.
- **Duration of Totality:** Up to **4 minutes and 8 seconds** (longest near the Galápagos Islands).

### Other Notable Eclipses Before 2000:
- **October 24, 1995** – Total Solar Eclipse (visible in **South Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific**).
- **November 3, 1994** – Total Solar Eclipse (visible in **South America**).
- **July 11, 1991** – Total Solar Eclipse (one of the longest of the 20th century, visible in **Hawaii, Mexico, and Central/South America**).

If you're looking for the **last solar eclipse of any type** (not just total) before 2000, it was an **annular solar eclipse** on **August 22, 1998** (visible in **Southeast Asia and the Pacific**).
